Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

dimensions.assessment: Affects low-income parents in postsecondary education receiving child care support through the CCAMPIS program, as well as federal personnel at ED and HHS.
dimensions.evidence: transfers specified functions relating to child care access for eligible low-income parents in postsecondary education from the Department of Education (ED) to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

dimensions.assessment: Administrative relocation of an existing program and its staff without altering underlying benefit structures or eligibility for applicants.
dimensions.evidence: The transfer of these functions does not affect any suits, proceedings, or applications for benefits, services... that are pending on the date of this bill's effective date.

dimensions.assessment: Transfers existing unexpended balances of appropriations and funds, with a requirement from OMB that the transfer causes no net increase in full-time equivalent employees.
dimensions.evidence: Unexpended funds transferred pursuant to this section shall be used only for the purposes for which the funds were originally authorized and appropriated.

dimensions.assessment: Involves an inter-agency transfer of statutory authorities, personnel, records, and administrative oversight responsibilities for a specific education program to a different cabinet-level department.
dimensions.evidence: There are transferred to the Secretary of Health and Human Services... all functions which the Secretary of Education exercised... under section 419N of the Higher Education Act of 1965

dimensions.assessment: Permanent administrative restructuring of program management taking effect 6 months after enactment or earlier.
dimensions.evidence: this Act shall take effect 6 months after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Exact dollar amount of appropriations and precise number of personnel being transferred.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill transfers the CCAMPIS child care program for low-income student parents, along with its personnel, assets, and appropriations, from the Department of Education to the Department of Health and Human Services.
